statement: For every such maxHeights, the function returns a result r and r is the maximum over all integer sequences heights of length n of sum_{i=0}^{n-1} heights[i], subject to: (i) 1 <= heights[i] <= maxHeights[i] for every 0 <= i < n; and (ii) heights is a mountain, meaning there exists a peak index p with 0 <= p < n such that heights[j-1] <= heights[j] for every 1 <= j <= p and heights[k+1] <= heights[k] for every p <= k < n-1. Thus heights is nondecreasing up to p and nonincreasing from p onward.
preconditions: n = len(maxHeights), 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= maxHeights[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: For every such maxHeights, the Lean function returns a success value r rather than failing; no arithmetic overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic occurs during the call.
preconditions: n = len(maxHeights), 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= maxHeights[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: For every such maxHeights, the function returns a result r and r <= sum_{i=0}^{n-1} maxHeights[i].
preconditions: n = len(maxHeights), 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= maxHeights[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: For every such maxHeights, let M = max_{0 <= i < n} maxHeights[i]. The function returns a result r and r >= M + n - 1.
preconditions: n = len(maxHeights), 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= maxHeights[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: For every such maxHeights, let m = min_{0 <= i < n} maxHeights[i]. The function returns a result r and r >= n * m.
preconditions: n = len(maxHeights), 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= maxHeights[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: For every such maxHeights, the function returns a result r and there exists an integer sequence heights of length n such that: (i) 1 <= heights[i] <= maxHeights[i] for every 0 <= i < n; (ii) heights is a mountain, meaning there exists p with 0 <= p < n such that heights[j-1] <= heights[j] for every 1 <= j <= p and heights[k+1] <= heights[k] for every p <= k < n-1; and (iii) sum_{i=0}^{n-1} heights[i] = r.
preconditions: n = len(maxHeights), 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= maxHeights[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: For every such maxHeights, the function returns a result r and for every integer sequence heights of length n that satisfies (i) 1 <= heights[i] <= maxHeights[i] for every 0 <= i < n and (ii) heights is a mountain in the sense above, one has sum_{i=0}^{n-1} heights[i] <= r.
preconditions: n = len(maxHeights), 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= maxHeights[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: For every such maxHeights, the function returns a result r and r = sum_{i=0}^{n-1} maxHeights[i].
preconditions: n = len(maxHeights), 1 <= n <= 100000, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= maxHeights[i] <= 1000000000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n-1, maxHeights[i] <= maxHeights[i+1].

statement: For every such A and B, the function returns results r_A on A and r_B on B, and r_A <= r_B.
preconditions: A and B are Slice Std.I64 values with the same length n, 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= A[i] <= B[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: For every such maxHeights, let rev be the length-n Slice defined by rev[i] = maxHeights[n-1-i] for 0 <= i < n. Let r and r_rev be the results returned by the function on maxHeights and rev respectively. Then r = r_rev.
preconditions: n = len(maxHeights), 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= maxHeights[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Let scaled be the length-n Slice with scaled[i] = c*maxHeights[i]. Let r and r_scaled be the results returned by the function on maxHeights and scaled respectively. Then r_scaled = c*r.
preconditions: c is a positive integer, n = len(maxHeights), 1 <= n <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= c*maxHeights[i] <= 1000000000.
